source_defaults.notes: Candidate-authored questionnaire responses, read in full answer context. Original publication and revision dates precede the primary. Assertions about accomplishments, opponents or policy effects remain attributed statements, not independent factual findings.

sources.speaker: Kaegan Marie Mays-Williams
sources.identity_notes: The publisher names Kaegan Mays-Williams as the NY Senate21 candidate, matching the canonical candidate with an additional middle name. This is an explicitly reviewed same-office public-name association.

statements.quote: reforms to rent control, and restoration of TOPA rights
statements.claim: Combines rent-control reform, restored tenant purchase rights, deeper affordability requirements, supportive housing and investment in the Housing Production Trust Fund and Local Rent Supplement Program.

statements.quote: Cure the Streets Violence Interrupters program
statements.claim: Names bringing Cure the Streets violence interrupters to Ward4 as the immediate public-safety priority, with emergency legislation and funding.

statements.quote: free transfers between bus and rail
statements.claim: Supports free bus-rail transfers within a faster, more reliable and accessible transit system.

statements.quote: I’m not taking any donations from corporations or developers
statements.claim: Connects public campaign financing and refusal of corporate/developer donations to an ability to fight for families and hold government accountable.

statements.quote: Housing Production Trust Fund
statements.claim: Presents annual Housing Production Trust Fund investment, new or preserved homes, public-housing repairs and senior housing as the basis of his affordable-housing approach; these are self-reported accomplishments.

statements.quote: I funded additional violence interrupters
statements.claim: Expresses support for and describes funding violence interrupters, alongside policing, task forces and nuisance-property enforcement. He does not present a policing-only approach.

statements.quote: eliminates fares, expands routes
statements.claim: Supports a fare-free expanded DC Circulator and subsidized WMATA fare cards.

statements.quote: strong relationships with my colleagues and the Mayor
statements.claim: Presents procedural knowledge, relationships and committee roles as means to deliver for Ward4.

statements.quote: replicated and integrated into redevelopment plans
statements.claim: Proposes replicating the Emory Beacon of Light affordable-housing development model at the former Walter Reed site. Her stated income threshold is not converted into an assumed AMI level.

statements.quote: increased community policing
statements.claim: Proposes foot and bike patrols, satellite police stations, an Officer Friendly school program and structured community-police coordination.

statements.quote: necessary staffing requirements
statements.claim: Proposes funding for teachers and auxiliary school staff, including nurses, social workers, psychologists and aides, plus learning technology.

statements.quote: helping hundreds of families navigate the public social service system
statements.claim: Presents experience helping residents navigate services and building relationships across agencies as preparation for the Council. This is a campaign self-description.

statements.quote: I totally and unequivocally support the New York Health Act
statements.claim: Supports the New York Health Act and describes an inside-outside organizing strategy to pass it; does not rely on his criticism of Parker as proof of Parker's policy stance.

statements.quote: Yes and yes.
statements.claim: Explicitly answers yes to single payer and co-sponsoring the New York Health Act; connects healthcare access to gun-violence prevention.

statements.quote: immediately cosponsor legislation banning evictions without good cause
statements.claim: Supports and would immediately co-sponsor Good Cause Eviction protections.

statements.quote: Yes.
statements.claim: Answers yes to co-sponsoring the Good Cause Eviction legislation asked about in the immediately preceding paragraph62.

statements.quote: eliminating wasteful giveaways to developers
statements.claim: Prefers ending 421a and485a abatements; if repeal lacks support, would seek strong affordability and worker-pay conditions as a fallback.

statements.quote: I would end it
statements.claim: Would end421a and seek affordable-housing solutions without a developer tax break.

statements.quote: I will proudly co-sponsor both pieces of legislation
statements.claim: Commits to co-sponsoring both Fair and Timely Parole and Elder Parole, which are specified in the preceding questions.

statements.quote: passing the Good Cause Eviction bill
statements.claim: His complete top-three-issues answer identifies housing, healthcare and climate, with specific bills and publicly controlled renewable energy.

statements.quote: Gun violence prevention.
statements.claim: Her complete top-three-issues answer names gun-violence prevention, affordable childcare and caregiver pay, and food insecurity, linked by a prevention-oriented public-health frame.

statements.quote: sex workers deserve a full decriminilization
statements.claim: Supports full sex-work decriminalization and opposes the Nordic model; original source spelling is preserved.

statements.quote: Full decriminalization is critical
statements.claim: Supports full sex-work decriminalization and argues that partial criminalization leaves workers vulnerable; not a medical or legal endorsement by this study.

comparisons.analysis: Lewis George emphasizes tenant protections, deeper affordability and expanded public investment; Todd emphasizes housing delivery and funding already secured. Both discuss the Housing Production Trust Fund positively, so the evidence does not support a simple pro-/anti-public-housing split.

Both favor violence-interruption programs. Lewis George gives Cure the Streets immediate priority; Todd combines interruption funding with police and other measures. Lewis George's non-answer to the vice-squad portion is not opposition.
Lewis George names free bus-rail transfers; Todd names fare-free Circulator service and WMATA fare subsidies. These affect different service and fare structures and can coexist.

Lewis George emphasizes independence from corporate/developer donors and accountability; Todd emphasizes experience and working relationships inside government. Neither campaign's claims about the other's motives or record are treated as verified facts.

Lewis George outlines a broad tenant-protection and public-investment program; Edwards emphasizes replicating a particular affordable-development model at Walter Reed. No unsupported comparison between household-income and AMI thresholds is made.

Lewis George foregrounds trained civilian violence interrupters; Edwards foregrounds community policing, patrols and police-school relationships. This is a contrast in proposed interventions, not an inferred categorical rejection of all other safety measures.
Lewis George emphasizes donor independence and challenging insiders; Edwards emphasizes service navigation and cross-agency coalition experience.
Both explicitly support single payer through the New York Health Act. Mays-Williams's support must not be inferred away from her former-prosecutor background or her separate parole qualifications.
Both support co-sponsoring Good Cause Eviction protections. Mays-Williams's short affirmative is bound to the specific preceding question.
Both prefer ending421a. Alexis separately describes stronger conditions as a fallback if repeal cannot pass; the shared preferred position does not erase that legislative qualification.

Alexis commits to co-sponsoring Fair and Timely Parole; Mays-Williams is unsure about the bill as written and seeks amendments. Her qualified answer is not categorical opposition to parole or rehabilitation.

Alexis organizes his lead priorities around housing, healthcare and climate; Mays-Williams around gun-violence prevention, childcare and food security. Their policy overlap, including healthcare and tenant protections, remains explicit.
Both favor full sex-work decriminalization and oppose the Nordic model in their own explanatory answers.
